To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enactment mechanism can infer process state by examining the state and history of the products created or modified by the actor, that this mechanism can also infer the knowledge level of a particular actor, and that this knowledge level can be taken into account by the enactment mechanism to provide guidance to the actor.

1) a descriptive enactment approach provides the necessary guidance without prescribing actions, and 2) a process state inference mechanism enables a descriptive enactment approach to work without requiring actors to notify the system about every action performed during process execution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an intelligent process enactment mechanism that can provide appropriate support for knowledge intensive processes.
the development of process support systems that provide the right amount of guidance, based on the level of knowledge of the user.
providing process support for knowledge intensive work in the form of a system that infers process state based on the state of products and provides guidance to actors only when needed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enactment mechanism is able to infer the state of a process from the products created or modified by the actors during the execution of that process.
the system is able to infer the state of the actor's knowledge and the state of the work process, and provide the actor with guidance when appropriate.
the proposed approach is a process state inference mechanism for support of knowledge intensive work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach to support process state inference, and have demonstrated that the approach is effective in supporting knowledge intensive work.

we are trying to provide a support mechanism for knowledge intensive work that is based on the idea that actors are the experts and the system should only support them when they need it, rather than forcing them to work in a certain way.
we have developed an enactment approach that supports the knowledge-intensive work of a process by inferring the state of the work process and providing appropriate guidance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the system can infer process state from the state of products produced during the process execution, rather than relying on actors to notify the system at every step.
process enactment can be made more flexible and adaptive by using a descriptive enactment approach.
